blocks.text: Every debt comes due in its own season.

blocks.alt: A sagging wooden gate at the edge of an unpruned orchard, moths circling in the last light.

blocks.text: The gate hangs on one hinge, half-swallowed by an orchard nobody prunes anymore. Somewhere past the trees, something is keeping *count*.

choices.text: Slip around the back, into the orchard

blocks.text: An old woman answers before you've finished knocking, lamp already lit, like she'd been standing there since dusk.

choices.text: Tell her the truth — you owe the Moth King
Lie and say you're only passing through

blocks.text: She doesn't smile, exactly, but something in her shoulders eases. "Go on, then," she says, and steps aside. "He prefers the honest ones. Doesn't make it easier on them."
She looks at you the way you look at a debt you already know you owe. "Passing through," she repeats, flat. But she steps aside anyway.
The fence gives easily where the wood has rotted. No one sees you go in, which feels, somehow, like the wrong kind of luck.
Moths lift off every branch you pass, thick as smoke. Somewhere under all that wingbeat, you can feel him counting. You owe the Moth King *{debt}* nights of light, and the season is nearly out.

blocks.alt: Rows of gnarled orchard trees thick with pale moths, dusk light through the branches.
blocks.caption: The orchard keeps its own kind of ledger.

choices.text: Pick up the lantern lying in the grass
Go straight to the King's tree

blocks.text: It's cold to the touch, and lighter than it looks — like whatever used to burn in it left in a hurry.
THE MOTH KING UNFOLDS FROM THE BARK.
*{debt}* nights, he says, in a voice like paper tearing. He does not ask what you've brought. He waits to see if you understand that he already knows.

choices.text: Offer to spend a season trimming the orchard

set.value: a season spent trimming the orchard

choices.text: Offer the lantern to relight his ledger
Beg him to forgive the debt outright
choices.lockedText: He only listens to those who came here honestly.

choices.text: Try to slip away without paying

blocks.text: He accepts with a single dry nod, and just like that the counting in the air goes quiet.

choices.text: Walk back through the orchard at dawn

blocks.text: The lantern catches the instant it touches his ledger, and for a moment the whole orchard is lit from underneath, every moth at once.

choices.text: Walk back through the orchard, {promise} behind you

blocks.text: He studies you a long moment — long enough that you start counting your own heartbeats — then exhales something that might be a laugh.

choices.text: Walk back through the orchard, forgiven

blocks.text: You get exactly as far as the gate before the first moth lands on your wrist. Then the second. Then you stop counting.
You gave him {promise}, and the moths lift off the branches all at once, like a held breath finally let go.
You gave him {promise}, and he took it the way anyone takes a fair trade — without ceremony, and without forgiveness either. The debt is paid. Nothing is forgiven. That was never on offer.
The Moth King does not raise his voice. He doesn't need to. By the time you understand what you've lost, the orchard has already stopped counting — because there's nothing left of the debt to count.
